title: Secure Blender MCP Server
description: Build a secure, tested Blender MCP server for isometric RTS sprite production. Replaces ahujasid/blender-mcp with purpose-built tooling for Roots of Reason asset pipeline. Key requirements: no arbitrary code execution, socket authentication, 95% code coverage, typed command whitelist, isometric rendering pipeline.

title: End-to-end integration tests
description:
Create integration tests that verify the full pipeline works end-to-end with mocked Blender.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Mock Blender server that responds to all whitelisted commands with realistic responses
- [ ] E2E test: connect -> setup scene -> render 8 directions -> process sprites -> validate output
- [ ] E2E test: authentication handshake -> command execution -> graceful disconnect
- [ ] E2E test: error scenarios (Blender crash mid-render, invalid model path, auth failure, timeout)
- [ ] E2E test: MCP tool invocation round-trip (tool call -> protocol -> mock Blender -> response)
- [ ] Fixtures: small test .blend file or mock scene data for render tests
- [ ] CI runs integration tests as separate step (can be slow)
- [ ] All integration tests pass in CI without real Blender installed
- [ ] Test coverage >= 95% maintained across all source files

title: Project scaffolding and CI
description:
Set up the Python project structure, dev tooling, and CI pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] pyproject.toml with all dependencies (mcp[cli], pytest, pytest-cov, pytest-asyncio, ruff, mypy)
- [ ] src/blender_tools/ package with __init__.py exposing version
- [ ] tests/ directory with conftest.py containing shared fixtures
- [ ] GitHub Actions CI workflow: pytest (95% coverage gate), ruff lint+format, mypy strict
- [ ] Makefile with test, lint, format, typecheck targets
- [ ] CLAUDE.md with project conventions
- [ ] Initial commit passes all CI checks
- [ ] Coverage >= 95% enforced in pyproject.toml

title: Authenticated socket protocol
description:
Implement the TCP protocol layer between MCP server and Blender addon with authentication and message framing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Length-prefixed JSON message framing (4-byte big-endian length header + UTF-8 JSON body)
- [ ] HMAC-SHA256 authentication handshake: server sends challenge, client responds with HMAC(shared_secret, challenge)
- [ ] Shared secret loaded from env var BLENDER_TOOLS_SECRET or auto-generated to temp file on first run
- [ ] Connection rejected with clear error if auth fails
- [ ] Async send/receive with configurable timeout (default 30s)
- [ ] Graceful handling of connection drops (reconnect on next command)
- [ ] Protocol unit tests: valid auth, invalid auth rejected, malformed messages rejected, timeout behavior, oversized message rejected (max 10MB)
- [ ] Test coverage >= 95% on protocol.py
- [ ] No use of eval(), exec(), or pickle anywhere in the protocol layer

title: Command registry and dispatch
description:
Implement the typed command whitelist — the core security boundary that replaces arbitrary exec().

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CommandRegistry class that maps command names to handler functions with typed parameter schemas
- [ ] Each command defined as a dataclass with typed fields (no **kwargs or untyped dicts)
- [ ] register_command(name, handler, param_schema) method
- [ ] dispatch(name, params) -> Result validates params against schema before calling handler
- [ ] Unknown commands rejected with CommandNotFoundError
- [ ] Invalid parameters rejected with ValidationError listing specific field failures
- [ ] Commands return structured CommandResult(success: bool, data: Any, error: str | None)
- [ ] Registry is frozen after initialization (no dynamic registration at runtime)
- [ ] Unit tests: register + dispatch, unknown command, invalid params, schema validation, frozen registry
- [ ] Test coverage >= 95% on commands/registry.py

title: MCP server with stdio transport
description:
Implement the MCP server that exposes Blender tools to Claude Code via stdio transport.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] MCP server using mcp[cli] SDK with stdio transport
- [ ] Server registers tools dynamically from command registry
- [ ] Each tool has typed input schema matching its command dataclass
- [ ] Tool execution: validates input -> sends command via protocol -> returns structured result
- [ ] Server handles Blender connection lifecycle (connect on first tool call, reconnect on drop)
- [ ] Proper error propagation: Blender errors become MCP tool errors with clear messages
- [ ] Server startup logs version, connection status (no secrets in logs)
- [ ] Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM
- [ ] Unit tests with mock protocol layer (no real Blender needed)
- [ ] Integration test: tool registration, tool listing, tool execution round-trip with mock
- [ ] Test coverage >= 95% on server.py

title: Blender addon socket server
description:
Implement the Blender-side addon that receives commands over TCP and executes whitelisted operations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Blender addon with bl_info metadata, installable via Blender preferences
- [ ] TCP socket server running in a background thread (non-blocking to Blender UI)
- [ ] Accepts authenticated connections using the same HMAC handshake as protocol.py
- [ ] Command dispatch: receives command name + params, looks up in local whitelist, executes via Blender API
- [ ] Only whitelisted commands execute — unknown commands return error, never eval/exec
- [ ] Thread-safe command execution: commands that modify scene run on main thread via bpy.app.timers
- [ ] Configurable port (default 9876) via addon preferences
- [ ] Status indicator in Blender UI (connected/disconnected)
- [ ] Addon unit tests (testable without running Blender via mock bpy)
- [ ] Test coverage >= 95% on addon Python files
- [ ] No hardcoded API keys, tokens, or secrets anywhere

title: Scene setup commands
description:
Implement commands for setting up Blender scenes for isometric sprite rendering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] setup_isometric_camera command: places camera at correct isometric angle (30deg elevation, 45deg rotation), orthographic projection, configurable scale
- [ ] setup_lighting command: configurable 3-point lighting setup optimized for sprite rendering (key, fill, rim)
- [ ] set_render_settings command: resolution, transparent background, output format (PNG with alpha), color depth
- [ ] import_model command: imports .blend, .obj, .fbx, .glb files into scene, returns object names
- [ ] clear_scene command: removes all objects except camera and lights
- [ ] apply_material command: applies material to object by name, supports player color mask (magenta #FF00FF)
- [ ] All commands validate parameters and return structured results
- [ ] Unit tests with mock bpy for each command
- [ ] Integration test: setup_camera -> setup_lighting -> set_render -> verify scene state
- [ ] Test coverage >= 95% on commands/scene.py

title: Isometric render commands
description:
Implement commands for rendering isometric sprites with correct canvas sizes for Roots of Reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] render_isometric command: renders current scene to file at specified resolution, returns output path
- [ ] render_directions command: renders 8 directions (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW) by rotating model 45deg between each, returns list of output paths
- [ ] render_animation command: renders animation frames for a given action/direction, returns frame paths
- [ ] Canvas size lookup from building footprint (1x1=128x128, 2x2=256x192, 3x3=384x256, 4x4=512x320, 5x5=640x384)
- [ ] Output naming convention matches Roots of Reason: {name}_{direction}_{frame:02d}.png
- [ ] Transparent background (RGBA PNG)
- [ ] Render parameters: samples, resolution_percentage, file_format all configurable with sensible defaults
- [ ] Unit tests with mock bpy and mock render output
- [ ] Test coverage >= 95% on commands/render.py

title: Sprite post-processing pipeline
description:
Implement commands that integrate with Roots of Reason's sprite processing pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] process_sprite command: takes rendered image path + building name, downscales to correct canvas size based on footprint, preserves magenta mask
- [ ] validate_sprite command: checks sprite dimensions, transparency, magenta mask presence, returns pass/fail with details
- [ ] batch_process command: processes all rendered images in a directory, returns summary of results
- [ ] Magenta mask restoration: after downscaling, snaps blended pink/purple pixels back to pure #FF00FF (same algorithm as Roots of Reason process-sprite)
- [ ] Output paths follow Roots of Reason convention: assets/sprites/buildings/placeholder/{name}.png
- [ ] Pillow used for image processing (lazy import with clear error if not installed)
- [ ] Unit tests with real small test images (committed to repo as test fixtures)
- [ ] Test coverage >= 95% on commands/sprite.py
